key_insight: A single, scalable training recipe yields consistent forecast-quality gains across model sizes from 4M to 2.5B parameters, demonstrating that time-series foundation models can be reliably scaled. Toto 2.0 (five open-weight models) sets new SOTA on multiple benchmarks.
problem_solved: Enables reliable scaling of time-series forecasting models — improving accuracy, robustness to contamination, and generalization across diverse forecasting benchmarks without bespoke tuning for each model size.
method: Develop a unified training recipe that transfers across model sizes and data regimes rather than tuning per-size.
Train a family of five open-weight forecasting models (Toto 2.0) spanning 4M to 2.5B parameters under that single recipe.
Evaluate extensively and demonstrate new state-of-the-art performance on BOOM (observability), GIFT-Eval (general-purpose), and TIME (contamination-resistant) benchmarks.
impact: Practitioners get a reproducible path to improve forecasting by scaling models with one training recipe and access to open-weight models for immediate use, fine-tuning, or production deployment — improving accuracy and robustness without extensive per-model engineering.
visual_elements: Performance vs. model size curve: line chart showing steady gains from 4M → 2.5B parameters across BOOM, GIFT-Eval, and TIME.
Recipe flow diagram: compact pipeline showing data preparation → unified training recipe → model family outputs (5 sizes) → evaluation.
Benchmark comparison bar chart: Toto 2.0 vs prior SOTA on BOOM, GIFT-Eval, TIME with percentage improvements annotated.
Robustness infographic: before/after contamination example showing Toto 2.0 maintaining accuracy where others degrade.
paper_title: Toto 2.0: Time Series Forecasting Enters the Scaling Era
paper_authors: Emaad Khwaja, Chris Lettieri, Gerald Woo, Eden Belouadah, Marc Cenac
